newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index up 0.34 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index up 0.34 pts.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in listless trading on Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with gains to refinery Slovnaft share pushing the index up 0.34 points to 208.68 points.
Brokers said they expected the current downward trend on the market to continue in the near future.

"Generally, the investors interest seems to be very small at the moment, and even if there is some, portfolio managers are not willing to sell at current low prices," Libor Chrast of ING Barings said.
The most heavily-weighted issue, refinery Slovnaft, closed up 14 crowns at 945, but traded only 62 shares on the bourse floor.
The country's largest commercial bank VUB continued in its weeklong decline, as it traded only one share, closing down 55 crowns at 1,780 crowns.
"The price in VUB, which peaked at some 2,300 crowns during the summer, had been boosted only by somebody's effort to achieve a larger stake," Chrast said.

"If now somebody would start to buy VUB in bigger volumes, it would be probably only on speculative reasons, since there exists a long-term risk of protfolio- restructuralisation and privatisation of the bank," he added.

Overall volume, boosted by settlements in direct OTC trades, climbed up to 3,246,301 shares, from 543,424 shares on Thursday, boosting turnover to 1.271 billion crowns. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687
